answer: Identity island cost curve. Each identity must anchor to a distinct attested device cluster; clusters sharing hardware fingerprints or network paths merge, so N synthetic identities cost one combined cluster. Attack cost scales superlinearly: the k-th additional identity in a cluster pays c·k^1.8 in fees and posting collateral. A falcon check flags clusters that rent fresh devices, charging them the full curve price. Sybils thus pay steeply rising marginal cost while honest lone agents stay on the cheap first step.
